# Alpine Demolition

> Commercial and industrial demolition contractor based in Arvada, Colorado. Full-scope structural demolition, environmental remediation, asbestos abatement, tank removal, material recovery, and disaster response for projects throughout Colorado.

## Company

- **Name:** Alpine Demolition
- **Type:** Commercial and industrial demolition contractor
- **Location:** 5790 W 56th Ave Suite C, Arvada, CO 80002
- **Phone:** 303-421-3366
- **Email:** jimmy@alpinedemolition.com
- **Service Area:** Colorado statewide — Denver metro, Fort Collins, Longmont, Aurora, Arvada, Boulder, Lakewood, Windsor, and surrounding areas
- **Years in Business:** Decades of documented Colorado project history

## Services

- Structural and mechanical demolition (commercial, industrial, government)
- Environmental remediation and abatement (asbestos, lead, mold, soil)
- Underground and above-ground storage tank (UST/AST) removal and purging
- Material recovery, deconstruction, and recycling
- Disaster and emergency site response (fire, wind, water damage)

## Notable Projects

- 990 Bannock (Denver Health Admin building, 100,000+ sq ft, 2019)
- Kodak Buildings Windsor (1,000,000+ sq ft industrial complex, 2014)
- Buckley Annex Lowry (3 government structures + asbestos abatement, 2014)
- Denver University Aspen Hall (39,000 sq ft, 2018)
- Sheraton Hotel Denver (12 acres, 615 rooms, 2010)
- Buckingham Mall Aurora (900,000 sq ft, 2008)
- Lory Apartments CSU Fort Collins (2012)
- Gove Middle School Denver (2012)
- Berthoud Bridge I-25 (infrastructure, 2012)
- JC Penney's Foothills Mall Fort Collins (active site, 2011)

## Safety

Alpine Demolition's health and safety program exceeds OSHA standards. Every project includes a site-specific safety plan, mandatory daily toolbox meetings, a dedicated health and safety officer on site, and management presence throughout. All staff are trained and equipped per task.

## Recycling Commitment

Alpine incorporates material recovery into demolition projects where site conditions allow — recovering steel, concrete, and wood for reuse or recycling. Recovery rates are documented at the project level.
